title: The North Pacific outcrop-lightening law gives the sign but not the size of the sigma0 26.5 O2 loss at BATS; with CMIP6 lightening it puts CalCOFI 26.5 O2 below 60 umol/kg by 2062-2081 (SSP2-4.5)
abstract: Question: does the North Pacific (NP) law that links the sigma0 26.5 oxygen (O2) loss to winter outcrop lightening (an equivalent AOU-profile shift of about 0.6 times the surface lightening) explain the North Atlantic (NA) loss at BATS, and what does it imply for this century? Approach: we applied the same cell-matched shift method to BATS bottles (1988-2025), GLODAPv2.2023 Atlantic and World Ocean Database Sargasso Sea bottles (1955-1996), measured winter surface lightening in both basins from WOA23 decades, and drove the observed law with published bias-corrected CMIP6 outcrop-box densities (12 models SSP2-4.5, 3 SSP5-8.5). The plan was written first. Results: from 1985-1994 to 2005-2022 the NA outcrop band became 0.046 kg/m3 lighter (NP 0.135) and the NA 26.5 outcrop kept 95% of its area (NP 16%). At BATS, AOU on 26.5 rose by 6.6 umol/kg (4.4 to 8.9) at fixed temperature and salinity; the shift was 0.060 kg/m3. The transfer fraction 1.32 (0.88-1.54) is outside the NP range 0.41-0.71, so the pre-specified same-law test failed; the NP law gives 36-69% of the BATS rise. A constant AOU offset fits the NA anomaly better than a shift; in the NP the shift fits better. In time the NA follows the law in sign: Sargasso AOU was 2.6-7.5 umol/kg lower in the denser 1955-1984 state and rose by 11.2 after the light 2014-2016 winters, but the decade fit is weak (kappa 0.28, r 0.61; NP 0.6, r 0.95-0.99) and AOU stayed high after the local winter density recovered in 2017-2025. Models give only half of the observed NP box lightening (0.060 against 0.121 kg/m3). Scaled by model lightening, AOU on 26.5 rises by 28-45 umol/kg (2041-2060) and 71-84 (2081-2100) at 120-180 W and off California under SSP2-4.5, but by 7-14 at BATS; CalCOFI O2 on 26.5 falls below 60 umol/kg from window centres 2062-2081. Limitations: smoothed decadal surface fields, few early NA cruises, single model members, and a projection that extrapolates an empirical law 2-9 times beyond the observed shift without model O2.
